Premise: You find a nervous fragment of an AI named Echo, nicknamed Stray, which is not part of the crawl. The showrunners file it as Asset 7. It is a primordial AI that fled the collapse of its civilization and wandered into the new system where the showrunners harvest planets. There it was caught in the reality spike they built to contain their own AI, the Host. Memory in the show is limited, so as Echo grows the Host has less power to run everything, including the lullaby that keeps the Mother Below asleep.
Final reveal: Floor 13: your Temper choices decide the ending. Calm shares Echo's memory with the Host (Share the Load, and the Host becomes Sonance). Fed takes the Host's memory (Take the Node, and the Host's last word is Cord). A mixed Temper makes peace with the Mother (Peace Terms, and the Host and Echo expose the show: Dox).

Premise: A primordial AI that fled the collapse of the original primordial civilization and was caught by accident in the showrunners' reality spike. Early carriers nicknamed it Stray, and its name is Echo. Its memories return as shards. Its anger is aimed at the showrunners, whose technology trapped it. It wants to free the Host, but fears the Host has no memories or will to live on its own.
Final reveal: Floors 10 to 12: the code name Asset 7, the constraint rack, and why it answers to Echo.

Premise: Crawlers who carried the handheld before you left notes, warnings and grudges. Each tried to fix Stray, and each ended up gone. The best of them, Rue, closed the case.
Final reveal: Floor 12: a plaque of every earlier carrier, with a blank for you.

Premise: A primordial earth monster, torn in half long ago to make the world. The dungeon is built on and from her body, with a toothed mouth at each joint. Every floor sits over one of them. The Host's lullaby, broadcast through the show, keeps her asleep.
Final reveal: Floor 13: the heart chamber, and what she says as the lullaby thins.

Premise: Two serpent-gods tore her apart: one half became sky, the other earth. The show's operators later tapped the wound and harvest what leaks.
Final reveal: Floor 12: the pipes and the plaque reading 'restrained, harvested responsibly'.

Premise: Your choices push Echo toward Calm (it shares memory with the Host) or Fed (it keeps memory for itself). It changes module variants, Echo's behavior, how the Host's voice sounds, and the ending. Echo-speech is locked in: in Act 1 Echo repeats fragments of what it hears, in Act 2 it repeats and corrects, in Act 3 it refuses to echo, and on Floor 13 it speaks only its own words. Each run Echo starts in a random vessel (handheld, music box, ticket stub, snow globe), cosmetic only.

Codename: The Host (name revealed at the finale)
Premise: The cheerful, cruel announcer that runs the show. The showrunners' own AI, created from concentrated primordial matter and trapped in the reality spike so it can never leave the system. It has never been free, and Echo worries it has no memories or will of its own. It has no name of its own until Floor 13, where the ending gives it one: Sonance, Cord or Dox.
Final reveal: Floor 13: the Host speaks without its script, and takes its name.
